amendments.body: crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:731-755, crates/tank_core/src/types/substrate.rs:24-36, and crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:220-225 do not actually derive SubstrateDeep area from current geometry. Scenario materialization stores colonizable_area_cm2 as footprint * factor (depth is ignored), the default layer hardcodes 100.0 cm², and the habitat registry then trusts that stored scalar verbatim. Two beds with the same footprint but different depths therefore get the same deep-substrate area, and TankState::new() reports the same 100 cm² regardless of tank size. That breaks the "geometry-derived colonizable area" contract for the habitat that downstream redox/biofilm systems are most likely to depend on.
amendments.rationale: This is a direct correctness bug in the new registry contract: downstream habitatized capacity/redox logic will be scaled from the wrong area on both default/manual states and any scenario that changes substrate depth.

amendments.body: crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:117 and 204-215 compute SubstrateSurface.light_exposure from geometry.mean_depth_cm(), and crates/tank_core/src/types/geometry.rs:60-62 defines that as fill_height_cm. Substrate thickness is therefore ignored: a shallow bed and a deep bed in the same tank get the same substrate-surface light even though the top of the deeper bed sits much closer to the lamp. The bead explicitly calls out depth/light context, so this misses one of the required sensitivities for the substrate habitat.
amendments.rationale: Later periphyton/root-zone systems will read this canonical light modifier and inherit the wrong attenuation whenever substrate depth changes.

amendments.body: crates/tank_core/src/types/habitat.rs:85-94 derives avg_crowding from the stored plant.crowding_index values, but crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:608-649 trims plant biomass without updating crowding, and crates/tank_core/src/types/state.rs:217-219 refreshes the habitat registry without recomputing crowding from the new biomass/footprint. After a large trim, PlantSurfaces area drops immediately but GlassHardscape/SubstrateSurface light exposure stays over-shaded until the next daily plant update. The registry is therefore still stale with respect to a plant-driven modifier even though it was just "refreshed."
amendments.rationale: This leaves the serialized habitat registry internally inconsistent after a common player action, which undermines the goal of having one canonical, inspectable source of habitat mechanics.

payload.summary: Reviewed the habitat-registry task changes across the engine/state/save/scenario wiring. I found three correctness gaps: deep-substrate area is still not fully geometry-derived, substrate-surface light ignores substrate depth, and plant-driven light shading can remain stale after biomass-changing actions because crowding is not recomputed.
